The speed setting seems to be applied to the entire game instead of just during battles. For example, if you switch it to 0.5x speed in order to gain a better understanding of your units and the enemies, it also slows things down after the battle is over. So you gotta increase it back to to 1x speed again. This isn't the way it should be. Surely those two should be completely separate. There's no way to zoom in. The units are tiny and the levels seem huge in comparison. Besides, it's a pity you can only have up to 6 units in your team. And only 1 equipment per unit. During battles, equipment doesn't show up on or around your units in any way either. Not even as icons or anything. Unstable FPS. Even during the tutorial. Even when you're basically not playing; e.g, when looking at the character recruitment screen. This is very unusual for an auto battler. Especially one made in Unity. Something isn't right.

Severely Imbalanced and Frustratingly Difficult I wanted to like Seer's Gambit, but after playing for a while, it became clear that the game is far from enjoyable. The class balance is a disaster. Some classes feel completely overpowered, while others are nearly useless. It’s frustrating to get a class and immediately realize that you stand no chance against certain enemies or challenges, no matter how well you play. It’s as if some classes were designed to be much harder to progress with, which makes no sense when you're trying to enjoy the game. On top of that, the difficulty spikes are insane. Even after purchasing all the upgrades in the region and grinding for hours, the game still feels ridiculously punishing. It’s like the developers designed the game with the assumption that you’ll have to spend more time endlessly grinding to even have a chance at progressing. It’s not fun; it’s just exhausting. You’re left feeling like you’re hitting a brick wall at every turn, which completely kills the sense of achievement. Overall, Seer's Gambit needs serious adjustments in both its class balancing and difficulty. Until then, it’s hard to recommend it to anyone who values a fair challenge over mind-numbing frustration.

The concept for the game is great, but the execution is poor. Situations can occur where enemies constantly spawn enemies and you constantly heal and you are basically in an infinite loop where nothing can progress. Multiple times I went to a new zone and the game just infinitely loaded and i had to close the program in order to continue. Oftentimes your starting units are just not strong enough to be able to fight even the first fight. You need to reroll multiple times to get units that are even usable in the endgame. If you don't start with an "epic" hero, you set yourself back completely. The combo system is great, but the icons for the combinations aren't shown automatically, so you have to a ton of clicking into menus to determine if any of your combos work. The game is completely unbalanced in the beginning and you have to lose multiple times before your units can even stay alive to progress. Then, if you ever accidentally hit "New Game" on the menu screen, it completely deletes any progress you have made. So basically I played for 7 hours of terrible unbalanced gameplay without any upgrades, and since I hit "New Game" I have to play through another 7 hours of unbalanced gameplay to play the game at all.

An autobattler with 6 units to use. Classes are Tank, healer, damage dealer/mage. Each class has different abilities and ultimate to use. Only 1 item slot for now, but the second one is coming soon. [h1]Pros: [/h1] - Different characters and builds to try out. - Sound effects match the fantasy style for a game with auto battles. [h2]Cons: [/h2] - Gold cost are too expensive for items. Reselling any item only gives 10 gold and even higher equipment only get 10 gold. Should be 15% of value if a better equipment. - No progression for losing except unlocking new characters for future runs. - Getting a strong build is too reliant on getting synergy via combos in shops and higher rarity party members. Combos give your abilities a boost, but you need 3 matching classes to get one. Re-rolling for shop characters is 30 gold each time, which is too high. [h3]Suggestions: [/h3] - The fights are hard to follow and camera angle is horrible. Spells are on the screen and you have control over casting ultimate spells, but you don't know if you are losing or winning until the fight is almost over. Why is the area for the cows taking up almost half the screen? - Placement for characters should be tank in front and healers in back automatically. Why make the player move units for each fight? - Shorten the runs or make the difficulty lower. It takes about 1 hour to level up your party and reach the harder areas. It's frustrating to restart with the slightly different build because the harder areas throw you into fights where enemies outscale you. - Give a difficulty rating for each area so its clear which path is more difficult to take. Losing because you chose a hard fight too early is not fun or rewarding. The Maw area is too hard and you get overwhelmed by spawned zombies/units. - Lack of balance and some characters are absolutely trash. Thief is too weak and needs to be buffed or removed. Due to lack of balance and difficulty, the game is not fun and restarting with no upgrades is frustrating. Give the option for an easy mode and update the combo/gold system to help the player. Saving the kingdom is a task the player is setup to fail and the tactics aspect is basically getting lucky rolls in character shops. [h2] 简短的评价，是个有点意思的游戏，但仅限于有点意思。 [/h2] [h3]个人评价：★★☆☆☆[/h3] 从休闲刷子游戏来看，前两三个小时确实蛮有意思的，羁绊加成、加点build、放置就能看着开打的自走棋制解压玩法，如果你是一开始抱着试探这个新奇游戏，那么确实非常能满足休闲玩家的心态。 [b]是什么时候感觉游戏开始变味的呢，当你打算进到这个世界认真玩的时候。[/b] 当你打算认真组个羁绊尝试走远点却发现d一个随从要30块钱根本没钱d的时候，当你辛辛苦苦组了个感觉很牛的阵容连boss的第一阶段都打不过去的时候，当你前期侥幸打完四阶段boss却发现咦成就没解锁完打完立马开下一把了那这世界到底还有没有其他内容我在纠结还值不值得探索的时候，当你玩多几局发现局外加成才是游戏根本玩法到中后期随便捡几个金的数值都能上千随便通关的时候。 这个游戏的弊端就暴露得一览无余，空洞的[b]主线[/b]和[b]boss设计[/b]，成就点莫名其妙的[b]地图策划[/b]，数值极其不合理的[b]成长曲线[/b]，基本对中后期毫无帮助的[b]事件设计[/b]。 我的游戏体验止在前几个小时，后面将近十五个小时的时长我都在反反复复地开着越发简单的轮回，去探索着不存在的“作者的设计”，去找那几个该死的成就到底要打哪个地图点，我的脑子里只有“[i]快解放吧[/i]”。 总之，是个有点意思的游戏，我感谢它带给我前几个小时还算不错的游戏体验，但仅限于有点意思，说更直接点就是毫无深度。听说游戏也还在开发和更新，对国人态度也比较好，基于此也值得一个人情上的好评，希望能改好点吧。

Another Update: As the NR.1 Reviewer with the LONGEST playtime (hohoho), here I share some thoughts and strategies on the gameplay. 1. One game session is ONE map. You are supposed to progress through the map and level up by unlocking more nodes. That means failure is guaranteed at early stages -- it's okay, nothing to lose and you still earn related currencies. The only way to NOT progress is to RESTART the current run before you fail. Accept failure, and move on. 2. Once you open enough nodes, it's fun time to experiment different builds. I know there are characters that "permanent gain X stat" and that seems like the only correction choice. WRONG. For normal session, a lot of characters are super strong with just their original stats + skill tree stats. For example, Icemalada, she can get her ability cooldown reduced to 2 sec with 100 ability stat from JUST the skill tree. Absolute queen and she's goat without combination or strong weapon already; another example, the arch guy (sorry, 100 hours and I remembered 0 names), he can get his attack to 1 sec CD with guaranteed crit. GOAT. They are fine to pick up even at the last round as their growth curves peaks up in a short time. 3. There are characters that MUST BE GROWNED at early stages, for example, the blond bob hair Nobel woman (again, name forgotten). Only get her if she's golden and level her immediately to the last skill tree. Her ability increases permanently in X-melee you own and she can both heal and dps at the same time with crazy stats. Useless to pick up if not gold or at later stage, as her raw stat is pretty meh. STRATEGY: ---- Tank will not tank unless it can taunt, healer will not heal unless it can survive, and melee DPS needs to have high move speed to target distant mobs. Always think about the survival of your support characters. Anyone that can pull, throw away, or invulnerable your healers are incredibly valuable. ---- AOE matters. Make sure you have characters that can reach and clean up the little mobs FAST. There is a mushroom that multiplies itself in insane rate, or mobs that spread very far apart. Your strong single-target DPS will die. ---- TEAM composition: safest team is 2 healer, 2 dps and 2 tank. More OP if each character can take up multiple roles. Some best DPS is your healer (go figure haha) ---- Growth space: some character will grow too fast and end the fight way too quickly, leaving no space for others to gain stats through fighting. Make sure your team growth is balanced by disabling ultimates, adjust CD with weapons, etc... FUN BUILDS (Now we are talking): ---- POISON: the most fragile but most intense DPS. With one thorn girl, she will permanently increase her Attack and apply poison to all [Ally ]. Poison accessories are easily available, and multiple characters with poison skill to assist her. It is not a SLOW BUILD. Do not build it to last long, the thorn girl has teeny-tiny health bar and she can get one-shot by range mobs. ---- NOBLES: the strongest team every. Forget about tanks, forget about healers, forget about dps. Throw all nobles on to the battlefield and they will show you want it means to be BETTER. Seriously. (For even better gameplay, get one thief guy for infinite money). ---- ALL HAIL THE FIRE QUEEN: yeah the queen that has fire ring around her, name forgotten again. To set her up, you need two elementalist (the fire icon), which comes from the wizard (really hard to play after the update), and the cloud girl (strong, but element-wise completely different to setup than the fire queen, you can really just pick one), and a spell element. I would say to set the fire up, the team will become a completely nonsense, but you will see, you will see, the fire queen conquers all ..... ---- ROOT: NO ONE APPROACH. Not only can both the IceQueen and the Arch guy root and deal high damage, at later stage you will unlock one character, that seems COMPLETELY USELESS until you set up a full range-root team. Congratulations, you have build yourself a rifle. No one can ever come close! enjoy! DIFFICULT BUILD: (still experimenting) ---- BLEED: the ability with the most single-target melee and ONE AOE -- the cloud girl. But to set her up to AOE [Bleed], oh so many elemental requirement! You need to get her to [crit], and that takes two dagger elements already. She is only a semi-healer, so now you need at least another strong healer that doesn't contribute to her [Bleed]-build. Now you have to take also one spot for the tank, and your team is full. Congratulations, it is not a good bleed team yet. The two dagger+ [Bleed] can only come from the blood-sucking girl, which is OP only when she does not use her [Bleed] build. You can also use the haircutter guy, but his only function is to give [crit] to cloud girl and randomly apply [Bleed]. So okay , but no one applies [Bleed] on a scalable stats, like poison from the Thorn girl, whose attack can grown infinitely. Another choice is the thief dagger guy that applies [attack] damage to every mob with [bleed], but you need to aoe blanket the mobs first, which is hard to do as mentioned before. ---- ALL TANKS. I believe it is possible to win with a team of only tanks. I am still trying. ---- ALL MUSHROOMS. I believe that Shroomherder is a 3-in-1: healer, tank and dps. I haven't got her to successfully take up the role as a healer, even though she is supposed to heal pretty frequently (maybe the fights are ending too soon before the mushrooms can reach the enemies). I need to play more on this. ---- BLIND: Blind in the base game is pretty meh as only one or two characters interact with this mechanics. But in the DLC it becomes relevant, I need to test it more often. I am really not sure if the game is intended to play as complicated as I am making it to be, but heh, I haven't gotten to the end of the endless mode yet, so clearly there is still room for growth! I haven't played autobattlers much, but I had good fun with this one. The team building combinations are engaging and you need to build your team around the first high rank heroes you meet in a run. During combat, some classes require you to time their ability well, while other can just auto cast their ultimate. I had a hard time putting the game down before my team met its demise. I'd only wish for more variety(events are recycled a lot for instance), but I am quite confident it will come soon as development is still pretty active.

Ehhhhhhhhhhh, on sale, but this is almost more akin to a flash game than a proper game. This game has all the makings of an amazing autobattler roguelite. It actually mirrors A LOT of what I wanted to make in a game myself. I am about to give a lot of criticisms but its out of love for the genre. The game is good, maybe buy it on sale but I'm THOROUGHLY enjoying it so far but feel like I'm burning through content too quickly. Before I tear it up, let me say I love the "play with the hand you're dealt" style adventures of building up a party and getting by with the options I have. I love finding synergies and building up heroes out of characters I doubted. I beat the cult (time limit boss) on my 4th run before I had cleared a single corrupted dungeon to open up the world more.. Now I'm just running around the map trying to clear it feeling like there's no final boss to care about anymore. Just because I hit a critical mass of armor/armor regeneration on 3 characters who just brute forced their way through the cult boss. Each hero is identical to others of the same type outside of their rarity. Another disappointing thing, every character is the exact same. Some sort of traits or random stats would have been amazing to lend different characters to different builds. One of the things I do enjoy from games like this is that heroes are just around. You'll run into 3 heroes every so often to pick from or not. This mirrors a game I wanted to make, coming across taverns with just some people inside. But it just doesnt feel great that EVERY Rogue is "the same guy" with the same stats and the same skill tree that can be molded into the same character that every other "Fingers the Thief" can become. I find that so limiting and unencouraging for future runs. Maybe races of each class could break it up. Perhaps some traits to alter their stats or change things up. Maybe random options on skill trees. Maybe a 4th row of skills that are random. I just doesnt feel great to still have to explore probably half of the map knowing nothing is really going to change unless I HOPEFULLY find more characters, but cant even see another tavern to reach in any direction. Its just discouraging and feels like I just have to grind now. I wish there was more variation between runs.

[h1]A fantastic game with surprising depth that's in desperate need of a balance patch.[/h1] Seer's Gambit isn't perfect, but it's good. If you enjoy roguelike autobattlers, this is worth the sale price of $15 and it's a steal at the (current) promotional price of $9.75. Almost every "problem" (and I use that term very lightly) with this game comes from a non-trivial amount of its content being useless because of how the rarity system works. [h3]The Good[/h3] There are just the right number of systems in play. Indie developers sometimes suffer from feature bloat, and I'm happy to say that is not the case here. Heroes synergize with each other in multiple ways, which usually means there is at least some synergy in your party of six. The sprites are pleasant, easy to interpret, and the visual effects are flashy without being overwhelming. The heroes are all thematically and mechanically distinct from each other. The game's few hints are impactful; I never felt at a loss for where to go or what I should be doing. Also, the game doesn't force you to play the objective. If you want to wander off and fulfill your own goals, you're not railroaded away from that. [h3]The Bad[/h3] The "Stats" page needs work. I would love if this was its own page and not a pop-up; there's a ton of good information in there that is made somewhat opaque by its lacking UI. Crit chance, especially, would benefit from living directly on a character sheet's "general" tab. Item and hero rarity has an immensely over-tuned impact on game balance. White/common rarity heroes and items are unusable, which would not be the worst if they were not omnipresent. One of the most interesting systems this game offers, "combos," is essentially removed from the game because of how white rarity heroes interact with the tag system. There are meta-progression updates that help mitigate this later, but this only partially solves the issue and only for those players who put tens of hours into the game first; so not great for the onboarding experience. Final boss spoilers: [spoiler]I've beaten the game several times and can say with confidence phase 3 is massively overtuned. It takes longer than all 3 other phases combined. Even with very strong squads on 4x speed, I can walk away from my computer for 5-10 minutes before the fight ends. My longest was a bit over 30 minutes. The problem is that there aren't enough global skills/items, and those that do exist don't trigger quickly or reliably enough to prevent healing.[/spoiler] [h3]The Needs Work[/h3] Rarity needs tweaking. White rarity either needs to be made usable or rare/epic needs to be more common. There's just...a lot of useless content in the current build and it's entirely because of rarity. Hero tags should be rarity agnostic. Combos are the most interesting part of the game by far, and the rarity system as it exists means a lot of the time combos just...don't exist as a system at all. I think tags being rarity agnostic would go a long way toward making some common content usable. Some heroes feel a lot rarer than others, and I'm not sure if that's intentional. Gloria and Celestine feel like they're in almost every shop; Rosa and Burnard show up so infrequently I forget they exist. 21 hours in I've never even seen an epic Rosa. [b]Balance in general.[/b] [*]Item usefulness is all over the place. Again, rarity is a factor here; almost all white items may as well not exist. [*]Combos are either ridiculously strong or complete nothingburgers. [*]Skills need tuned; some are obviously stronger than others. [*]There's a couple maps that are disproportionately punishing, and a few that are really really easy. [h3]The Verdict[/h3] It's good and you should play it. The only thing holding this game back is a balance patch.

看老菊玩才买的，自己玩真的不好玩，技能、事件、数值设计得都很简陋以及糟糕，为了打成就肝了几天，是我玩过的最不好玩的自走棋了 开发者留言后的补充： John你好，我觉得最大的问题是，整个游戏给人感觉设计得非常模糊，玩家并不了解数值的意义，比如升级加技能点，或者装上装备时都会有描述，提高了多少点什么能力，但是这些数值的提升在战斗中反馈完全不明显，即使玩了不少局，也很难清晰理解某个数值增长到底算不算强，怎样才算强。从观察对战来看，这些增长实际上恐怕也大都不强，又只能大概估计，就导致玩家的反馈感较弱。 还有，角色之间能力过于不平衡。这一点在无尽模式里尤为明显。事实上，在中文游戏社区，大多数玩家都是以爱斯梅拉达（冰女）为核心通关无尽模式第16轮的，还有少部分其他组合也非常有限。我印象很深的是曾经把理发师刷到了非常高的血量，然后在进入第十几轮以后迅速溃败，毫无继续的希望，这似乎在告诉玩家，许多你觉得有趣的、值得探索的阵容会被游戏彻底否定。为了达成全成就，我玩了很多局这样的游戏，然后在第十几轮输掉。这迫使玩家只能通过很有限的组合达成高难度胜利，而且要拼凑固定的羁绊又只能靠运气，给玩家的感觉并不好。大多数角色初看有明确的定位，但随着游戏进行而变得面目模糊，最后完全被玩家放弃，而且似乎制作者并没有意识到这个问题。 另外，上面说的第一点导致了大部分装备和许多技能变得毫无存在感，可有可无。在高难度游戏中，往往只需要一两个特定的装备（如爱斯梅拉达+蔑视之球），而低难度游戏中连这些装备也不重要了。许多装备和技能也缺乏除了“变强”以外的鲜明特点，尽管其中一些包含了各种词条。 总的来说，整个游戏给玩家的反馈不明显，而且如果做全成就的话会经历很多玩家明知道无用的时间（为了测试羁绊强度，为了随机出想要的、很有限羁绊和装备）。以上是我觉得大概存在的问题，也许也包含了一些个人主观的东西。我想，开发者既然能在意、询问玩家的感受，那就能逐渐做得更好，祝你们顺利。

Seer’s Gambit, developed by Unleash The Giraffe and published in collaboration with Gamersky Games, takes the familiar foundations of the auto-battler genre and reshapes them into a more deliberate, single-player roguelite experience. Instead of leaning into competitive multiplayer or rapid-fire decision-making, it slows the formula down and gives players room to think, experiment, and adapt. That shift in pacing is not just a minor tweak—it fundamentally changes how the game feels, transforming what is often a reactive genre into something more methodical and approachable without sacrificing its strategic depth. The gameplay loop centers on building a team of heroes and guiding them through a branching series of encounters. Each run presents a sequence of battles, events, and upgrade opportunities, with players constantly adjusting their composition based on what they encounter. Combat itself plays out automatically once units are placed on the field, but it doesn’t feel entirely hands-off. Each character builds energy over time and can unleash powerful abilities that the player activates manually, adding a layer of timing and engagement that keeps battles from becoming passive. This hybrid approach strikes a satisfying balance, allowing the player to influence the outcome without needing to micromanage every action. What gives Seer’s Gambit its staying power is how much emphasis it places on synergy and positioning. Characters belong to different archetypes, and combining them effectively unlocks bonuses that can dramatically alter a run. Placing units in the right positions—ensuring frontline durability, protecting fragile backliners, and maximizing area-based abilities—becomes just as important as choosing the right characters in the first place. The interplay between these systems creates a steady stream of small, meaningful decisions, encouraging players to experiment with different combinations and strategies. Success rarely comes from simply picking the strongest units; it comes from understanding how they work together. The roguelite structure reinforces this sense of experimentation by ensuring that every run contributes to long-term progress. Unlocking new characters, abilities, and upgrades gradually expands the pool of possibilities, giving players more tools to work with over time. Even failed attempts feel productive, as they often reveal new strategies or open up future options. This constant sense of progression helps maintain engagement, creating a loop that encourages repeated play without feeling overly punishing. It’s the kind of system that quietly builds momentum, drawing players back in with the promise of refining their approach and discovering new synergies. One of the game’s most notable design choices is its flexibility in pacing. Unlike many auto-battlers that unfold in real time with little room for pause, Seer’s Gambit allows players to slow things down and assess the situation at their own pace. This makes it far more accessible, especially for those who prefer thoughtful planning over quick reactions. It also reinforces the game’s identity as a strategy-focused experience, where decisions are made carefully rather than under pressure. This feature alone sets it apart from many of its peers and broadens its appeal to a wider audience. Visually, the game adopts a vibrant pixel-art style that complements its fantasy setting. The character designs are varied and expressive, giving each unit a distinct identity that makes team-building more engaging. While the environments are relatively simple, they serve their purpose without distracting from the action. The presentation as a whole feels cohesive, if not particularly ambitious, and aligns well with the game’s focus on clarity and readability during combat. Despite its strengths, Seer’s Gambit is not entirely without flaws. Balance can be inconsistent, with certain character combinations or archetypes outperforming others by a noticeable margin. This can occasionally limit the effectiveness of experimentation, as players may feel nudged toward specific strategies. Difficulty spikes can also disrupt the flow, particularly in later stages where encounters may require multiple attempts to overcome. Additionally, technical issues and minor bugs can appear from time to time, reminding players that this is still a relatively small-scale indie project. Even with these shortcomings, the game manages to carve out a distinct identity within a crowded genre. It doesn’t try to compete directly with the fast-paced, competitive nature of traditional auto-battlers, instead offering a more relaxed and introspective alternative. By focusing on synergy, progression, and player-controlled pacing, it creates an experience that feels both accessible and strategically engaging. In the end, Seer’s Gambit is a thoughtful and addictive reimagining of the auto-battler formula. It may not be perfectly balanced, and it shows signs of its indie roots, but its core ideas are strong enough to carry the experience. For players who enjoy experimenting with builds, refining strategies, and taking their time with decision-making, it offers a rewarding and refreshing take on the genre. Rating: 8/10

My thumbs down comes mainly from the game price. It isn’t a bad game, it just have 5 € fun in my humble opinion. The game basically a gambling idler. The player doesn’t have almost any meaningful tools in the runs. With the recent update you can select now your starting character, and your starting point on the map, if you’ve grinded long enough. Afterwards you travel based on the chosen node of the map. There are very limited travel types, and in every travel there are only few events in the mix. If you traveled even once of a the type, you’ve seen everything. Keep in mind, on the map there are many same type of travels, so even on your first run you’ll see the same content more than once. The battle has the same limited options. There are few battle maps in the pool during the travels. Each travel has a very limited selection of enemies, so again if you’ve played once, basically you saw most what the game can offer. During the battle you place your troops on limited spots, so that’s the strategy input from you. I played on 4x speed, but I was bored, because there are almost zero player agencies during the run. In theory it could’ve been fun to assemble various mix of heroes, but you’re extremely hindered by game design. The heroes come in 3 rarity, which limits the maximum level of the unit. So you have to hunt for the right kind of unit for your dream build in the epic version. I believe it’s extremely punishing to have 2 levels of RNG. You can re-roll the selection, but 30 gold isn’t cheap, and nothing guarantees that you’ll get better units. The „roguelike” part means that you have to come back and grind for eternity so you can buy minor upgrades. Game is super easy, but becomes really boring really fast.
